status.en: 165 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 29% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 165 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 29 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen have intensified attacks across northern Nigeria, killing police officers in Borno, Plateau and Sokoto-Gusau, and abducting police, students, worshippers, mourners and schoolchildren in Zamfara, Benue, Kaduna and Niger. Armed groups also shot a tin miner in Barkin Ladi, killed two miners in a pit collapse, and robbed a convoy on the Kaduna-Zaria highway. Bandits ambushed a police convoy in Zamfara and killed five officers on the Sokoto-Gusau highway. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpnede menn har økt angrepene i Nord-Nigeria, drept politifolk i Borno, Plateau og Sokoto-Gusau, og bortført politifolk, studenter, tilbedere, sørgende og skolebarn i Zamfara, Benue, Kaduna og Niger. Væpnede grupper skjøt også en tinnminer i Barkin Ladi, drepte to gruvearbeidere i en gruvekollaps, og ranet en konvoi på Kaduna-Zaria-veien. Banditter la en bakholdsangrep på en politikonvoi i Zamfara og drepte fem offiserer på Sokoto-Gusau-veien. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
